draft.title: Anode and cathode
card: the electrode where oxidation happens. The species there loses electrons.
the electrode where reduction happens. The species there gains electrons.
In a galvanic cell, electrons are released at the anode, so the anode is the negative electrode. They travel through the external wire to the cathode, which is positive.

Take a cell with zinc in Zn²⁺ solution and copper in Cu²⁺ solution. Zn(s) → Zn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ happens at the zinc electrode, so zinc is the anode. Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Cu(s) happens at the copper electrode, so copper is the cathode.
draft.remember: Oxidation at the anode, reduction at the cathode. In a galvanic cell the anode is negative.

a.q: In a galvanic cell, which statement about the anode is correct?
opts: Oxidation happens there and it is the negative electrode
Oxidation happens there and it is the positive electrode
Reduction happens there and it is the negative electrode
Reduction happens there and it is the positive electrode
a.why: Oxidation is loss of electrons, and it happens at the anode. These electrons make the anode the negative electrode in a galvanic cell. The option with reduction at the negative electrode mixes up the anode and the cathode.
a.clue: Electrons are released at the anode.

b.q: A galvanic cell has a nickel electrode in Ni²⁺(aq) and a silver electrode in Ag⁺(aq). Ni(s) is oxidised and Ag⁺(aq) is reduced. Which row is correct?
opts: Nickel is the anode; electrons flow from nickel to silver
Nickel is the anode; electrons flow from silver to nickel
Nickel is the cathode; electrons flow from nickel to silver
Nickel is the cathode; electrons flow from silver to nickel
b.why: Nickel is oxidised, so it is the anode. It releases electrons, which flow through the wire to the silver cathode, where Ag⁺ is reduced. Electrons flow from the anode to the cathode, so a flow from silver to nickel would be backwards.
b.clue: Find which electrode is oxidised, then follow the electrons from there.

a.best: Oxidation happens there and it is the negative electrode

b.best: Nickel is the anode; electrons flow from nickel to silver
